questions.stem: The 'Arthashastra', a comprehensive treatise on statecraft, economics, and military strategy, was authored by:
questions.explanation: The **Arthashastra** is attributed to **Kautilya** (also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta), the minister and advisor who helped Chandragupta Maurya establish the Mauryan Empire. Rediscovered in 1905 by R. Shamasastry, it covers administration, espionage, economics, and foreign policy in extensive detail.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which Greek ambassador was sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: **Megasthenes** was the Greek ambassador stationed at Pataliputra (Patna) in the court of Chandragupta Maurya. He authored the 'Indica', a detailed account of India's geography, people, and the Mauryan administration, though the original work survives only in fragments preserved by later Greek writers.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Ashoka's Kalinga War, which caused enormous suffering and transformed him into a proponent of Dhamma and non-violence, was fought around:
questions.explanation: Ashoka fought the **Kalinga War in approximately 261 BCE** (8th year of his reign). Rock Edict XIII records his deep remorse — approximately 100,000 killed, 150,000 deported — and his subsequent embrace of Buddhist Dhamma. 232 BCE was the year of Ashoka's death.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The capital of the Mauryan Empire was:
questions.explanation: **Pataliputra** (modern Patna, Bihar) was the capital of the Mauryan Empire. Megasthenes described it as a magnificent city on the confluence of the Ganges and Son rivers, surrounded by a massive wooden palisade with 570 towers and 64 gates.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Most of Ashoka's rock edicts in mainland India were inscribed in which script?
questions.explanation: Most Ashokan inscriptions in the Indian subcontinent are in **Brahmi** script (read left to right). Northwestern edicts (in Gandhara/Pakistan) use Kharoshti (right to left). The Kandahar edicts in Afghanistan use Greek and Aramaic. Brahmi was used for edicts in the Deccan, Orissa, and the Gangetic plain.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which Mauryan ruler immediately preceded Ashoka on the throne?
questions.explanation: **Bindusara** (r. c. 298–273 BCE) was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the father of Ashoka. He was known to the Greeks as 'Amitrochates' (destroyer of enemies). Bindusara extended Mauryan authority into the Deccan. He was a follower of the Ajivika sect.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Chandragupta Maurya is said to have abdicated his throne and accepted which religion at the end of his life, reportedly dying at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka)?
questions.explanation: According to Jain tradition, Chandragupta abdicated in favour of his son Bindusara and became a **Jain monk** under the guidance of saint **Bhadrabahu**. He migrated to Shravanabelagola (Karnataka) and died there through Sallekhana (ritual fasting). This is not mentioned in Hindu or Buddhist sources.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Greek account of ancient India that described Mauryan society and administration, authored by Megasthenes, was titled:
questions.explanation: Megasthenes wrote the **'Indica'**, which described India's geography, rivers, flora, fauna, the city of Pataliputra, the seven social classes of Indian society, and the Mauryan administration. The original is lost but reconstructed from fragments in Arrian's Indica, Diodorus Siculus, and Strabo.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Mauryan provincial unit below a province (administered by a royal prince/governor) and above a village was roughly equivalent to a district and called:
questions.explanation: The Mauryan administrative hierarchy ran: Empire → Province (headed by Kumara/Prince) → **Ahara** or **Vishaya** (district) → Grama (village). The Arthashastra mentions 'Ahara' and the edicts mention 'Rajuka' as the district-level officer responsible for welfare of rural populations.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Ashoka sent Buddhist missions to various regions. His son Mahindra was specifically sent to spread Buddhism in:
questions.explanation: Ashoka sent his son **Mahindra** (and daughter **Sanghamitra**) to **Sri Lanka** (Ceylon/Lanka) at the invitation of King Devanampiya Tissa. Mahindra converted the king and the island to Buddhism. Sanghamitra brought a sapling of the original Bodhi Tree to Anuradhapura, where it still grows.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Which Ashokan Rock Edict describes the horrors of the Kalinga War and Ashoka's subsequent remorse and conversion to Dhamma?
questions.explanation: **Major Rock Edict XIII** is the most detailed edict about the Kalinga War. Ashoka writes that 100,000 were killed, 150,000 deported, and many more died from disease and famine. He expresses remorse ('Beloved of the Gods feels remorse') and declares Dhamma-conquest superior to military conquest.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The primary silver/copper coin of the Mauryan Empire, mentioned in the Arthashastra, was called:
questions.explanation: The standard Mauryan coin was the **Karshapana** (also called 'Pana'), typically a silver punch-marked coin. Copper and gold variants also existed. The Arthashastra provides details of the monetary system, including the role of the Mint (Rupadarsaka).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The last Mauryan emperor, who was killed by his own commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Shunga during a military parade, was:
questions.explanation: **Brihadratha** was the last Mauryan emperor. Around 185 BCE, his commander-in-chief **Pushyamitra Shunga** assassinated him during a military parade, ending the Mauryan dynasty and founding the Shunga dynasty.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Ashoka's daughter Sanghamitra is particularly associated with which act that had lasting religious significance?
options: Bringing a sapling of the original Bodhi Tree to Sri Lanka (Anuradhapura)
Founding the city of Ujjain as a Buddhist centre
questions.explanation: **Sanghamitra** accompanied her brother Mahindra to Sri Lanka and brought a **sapling of the Bodhi Tree** (from Bodhgaya) to Anuradhapura. King Devanampiya Tissa planted it at the Mahamevnawa Garden; this Sri Maha Bodhi tree is considered the oldest historically documented tree in the world, still living today.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Ashoka's concept of 'Dhamma' primarily emphasized:
options: Animal sacrifice and Vedic rituals as state religion
Strict Buddhist monastic rules for all citizens
Tolerance, non-violence (Ahimsa), respect for all religions, and social welfare measures
Military conquest to spread Buddhism across Asia
questions.explanation: Ashoka's **Dhamma** was NOT sectarian Buddhism. It was a moral code emphasizing: **non-violence (Ahimsa)** toward all living beings, **religious tolerance** (respect for all sects), filial piety, compassion, truthfulness, and social welfare (hospitals for humans and animals, tree plantations, wells). Rock Edict XII specifically preaches tolerance.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Mauryan Empire reached its greatest geographic extent under which ruler?
questions.explanation: The empire reached its maximum extent under **Ashoka**, stretching from Afghanistan (Kandahar) in the west to Bangladesh in the east, and from the Himalayas in the north to Karnataka and Andhra in the south. Only Kalinga (Odisha) was outside it before the Kalinga War in 261 BCE.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Sarnath Lion Capital erected by Ashoka, featuring four back-to-back lions atop an abacus with wheels and animals, has been adopted as:
options: The logo of the Reserve Bank of India
The crest of the Indian Army
The symbol of the Indian Tourism Board
questions.explanation: The **Sarnath Pillar's Lion Capital** was adopted as the **National Emblem of India** on 26 January 1950. The four Asiatic lions face the four directions. Below the abacus are a horse (right), bull (left), elephant (far right), lion (far left), and dharma chakras. The motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is inscribed from the Mundaka Upanishad.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Chandragupta Maurya defeated which last ruler of the Nanda dynasty (known to the Greeks as 'Agrammes') to establish the Mauryan Empire?
questions.explanation: **Dhana Nanda** (Agrammes/Aggrammes to the Greeks) was the last and reportedly most powerful Nanda king of Magadha. Chandragupta Maurya, supported by Kautilya's strategy, defeated and overthrew him around **321–322 BCE**, founding the Mauryan Empire at Pataliputra.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Ashoka's edicts found at Kandahar (modern Afghanistan) are unique because they are written in which languages?
options: Greek and Aramaic (for the Greek and Iranian populations there)
questions.explanation: The **Kandahar edicts** (Shahbazgarhi and Kandahar) are written in **Greek and Aramaic** — catering to the Greek (descended from Alexander's settlement) and Iranian-speaking populations. This demonstrates Ashoka's attempt to communicate Dhamma to diverse linguistic communities within his vast empire.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Historians generally attribute the decline of the Mauryan Empire primarily to:
options: A series of devastating natural disasters
Invasion by the Kushana rulers from Central Asia
Buddhist pacifism weakening military strength alone
Weak successors after Ashoka causing administrative fragmentation, economic strain, and regional/Brahminical revolts
questions.explanation: Most historians attribute Mauryan decline to **weak post-Ashoka successors** who could not hold together the vast empire. Factors include: administrative fragmentation, economic strain from Ashoka's costly welfare programmes, rise of regional powers (Satavahanas, Greeks, Kalingas), and the eventual coup by Pushyamitra Shunga (185 BCE).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: In his 'Indica', Megasthenes described the social structure of Mauryan society as comprising seven 'castes' (actually occupational categories). Which of the following best matches his description?
options: Philosophers, soldiers, herdsmen, husbandmen/farmers, craftsmen, overseers, and councillors/advisors
Warriors, priests, merchants, artisans, servants, farmers, outcastes
Four varnas plus three additional occupational groups for mixed-caste offspring
Two classes: ruling aristocracy and working masses
questions.explanation: Megasthenes described **seven groups**: (1) Philosophers (Brahmins + Shramanas), (2) Farmers/husbandmen (largest group), (3) Herdsmen/hunters, (4) Craftsmen/traders, (5) Soldiers (second largest), (6) Overseers (government inspectors), (7) Councillors/assessors (King's advisors). Note: these are occupational, not the Hindu varna system.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The treaty between Chandragupta Maurya and the Seleucid king Seleucus Nicator (c. 305 BCE) resulted in which significant outcome?
options: Chandragupta became a vassal of Seleucus
Seleucus ceded eastern territories (trans-Indus regions) and gave his daughter in marriage, receiving 500 war elephants in exchange
A military alliance was formed to defeat the Ptolemies of Egypt
Seleucus conquered most of northwestern India
questions.explanation: After military conflict, the **treaty of 305 BCE** had Seleucus cede territories including Arachosia (Kandahar), Gedrosia (Balochistan), and Paropamisadae (Kabul region) to Chandragupta, along with giving his daughter (or a princess of the Seleucid house) in marriage. In exchange, Chandragupta gave **500 war elephants**, which Seleucus used decisively at the Battle of Ipsus (301 BCE).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The 'Separate Kalinga Edicts' (found at Dhauli and Jaugada in Odisha), unlike the corresponding Major Rock Edicts they replace, are significant because they:
options: Describe Ashoka's military campaigns after Kalinga
Are bilingual in Brahmi and Greek
Are specifically addressed to Ashoka's administrative officials in Kalinga about treating the newly conquered people with compassion and justice
Record exact casualty numbers from the Kalinga War
questions.explanation: The **Separate Rock Edicts I and II** at Dhauli and Jaugada replace Major Rock Edicts XI, XII, XIII (which are not found at these sites). They are addressed to the Mahamatras (officers) of Tosali and Samapa, instructing them to treat the people of Kalinga — now under Mauryan rule — with **paternal compassion, impartially and without harshness**, and to ensure their welfare.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Kautilya's Arthashastra describes the 'Mandala' (circle of states) theory. Under this doctrine of foreign policy, the fundamental principle is:
options: Always ally with the nearest neighbor
The enemy of your enemy is always an ally regardless of distance
Neutral states must be absorbed first before dealing with enemies
The immediate neighbour is a natural enemy; the state beyond the neighbour is a natural ally ('Ari-Mitra-Sandhi')
questions.explanation: The **Mandala theory** posits concentric circles of states around a central kingdom (Vijigishu). The immediate neighbor is a potential **enemy** (Ari), the neighbor's neighbor is a **natural ally** (Mitra). The system extends outward in alternating enemy-ally rings. This was a realist-pragmatic doctrine for strategic statecraft.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Minor Rock Edict I, found at Maski (Karnataka) among other sites, is unique in Ashokan inscriptions because it:
options: Describes the Kalinga War in the most detail
Was written in three scripts simultaneously
Explicitly mentions the name 'Ashoka' (the only edict to do so by name, helping scholars identify 'Devanampiya Piyadassi' as Ashoka)
Records the founding date of the Mauryan Empire
questions.explanation: Most Ashokan edicts refer to him only as 'Devanampiya Piyadassi' (Beloved of the Gods, Of Pleasing Countenance). The **Maski Minor Rock Edict I** (and a few others — Nittur, Brahmagiri, Udegolam) are the only ones that include the name **'Ashoka'** explicitly, enabling 19th-century scholars (James Prinsep et al.) to conclusively identify the author of the edicts.
questions.subject: History
